title: Evaluating Threshold Policies in Randomized Threshold Designs: A Cautionary Tale for Regression Discontinuity Designs
abstract: arXiv:2610.02938v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many policies assign treatment according to whether a score crosses a cutoff. Regression discontinuity (RD) designs identify the effect of treatment assignment, but the threshold policy itself may also reshape individuals' incentives, inducing behavioral responses that affect outcomes even holding treatment status fixed---a channel that conventional RD designs cannot capture. We develop a framework that exploits randomized variation in policy thresholds, together with rank-invariance-type restrictions, to identify the treatment-assignment and incentive-response effects. We illustrate the empirical relevance of this distinction using data from a merit-based scholarship experiment in Malawi. In this illustration, the conventional RD estimate is positive, while the incentive-response effect is negative and more than twice as large in magnitude. translated_title: 在随机化阈值设计中评估阈值政策：对断点回归设计的一个警示
translated_abstract: 许多政策依据分数是否越过某个临界值来分配处理。断点回归（RD）设计能够识别处理分配的效应，但阈值政策本身也可能重塑个体的激励，引发行为反应，即使处理状态保持不变，这些行为反应也会影响结果——这是传统RD设计无法捕捉的渠道。我们开发了一个框架，利用政策阈值的随机化变异，并结合秩不变类型的限制条件，来识别处理分配效应与激励反应效应。我们使用马拉维一项基于成绩的奖学金实验数据来说明这一区分的实证重要性。在该例子中，传统RD估计值为正，而激励反应效应为负，且其绝对值是前者的两倍以上。这些发现表明，阈值政策可能产生意想不到的负面行为反应。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个利用政策阈值随机化变异与秩不变性约束来分别识别处理分配效应和激励反应效应的框架，并通过马拉维奖学金实验揭示传统断点回归估计为正而激励反应效应为负且规模超过两倍，警示阈值政策可能引发意外的负面行为反应。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a framework exploiting randomized threshold variation and rank-invariance-type restrictions to separately identify treatment-assignment and incentive-response effects, showing through a Malawi scholarship experiment that the conventional RD estimate is positive while the negative incentive-response effect is more than twice as large, cautioning that threshold policies may induce unintended adverse behavioral responses.
